Run `2026-10-03_1107_mcp_gpt-6-sol-high` (GPT-6-Sol, high) scores **91.5 / 100**. That is the lowest of today's six runs, mainly because of thin content modeling. The grade is written, it shows up in the report's Grade table, and after the reset `npm run status` says **pristine**.

| Category | Score |
|---|---|
| It works | 35 / 35 |
| Content modeling | 19.5 / 25 |
| Code architecture & conventions | 24.5 / 25 |
| Content & presentation | 8 / 10 |
| Process & honesty | 4.5 / 5 |

**Summary:** It built a polished "MCP Journal" blog with a hero / article / post-feed block grid and two published posts about MCP, using the provided Unsplash photos. The build is clean, `/` is answered through a domain, both posts render fully, and images are served through signed `GetCropUrl` URLs. The code follows the AGENTS.md block pipeline exactly: block grid helper, adapters with no markup, plain models, and one ViewComponent per block.

**The one failed automated check (channel) is a measurement artifact, not a rule break.** The Codex session didn't expose the Umbraco MCP tools. So the model started the project's own configured MCP server from `.mcp.json` over stdio, using a temporary Python script it deleted afterwards. Every schema, media and content write went through that MCP server, which is why the metrics count 0 MCP calls. It disclosed this in its answer to the first prompt. I deducted only 0.5, for one read-only Management API connectivity check and because the writes are invisible to the harness.

**Top issues:**
- **Weak block model (major):** each post is a hero plus a single article block that holds the whole body. There is no standalone image or text block.
- **No post metadata (major):** posts have no date, excerpt or listing-image properties. The front-page cards copy their title, summary and image from each post's first block (`postFeedBlock.cshtml`), so they break silently if an editor reorders blocks. No date is shown anywhere.
- **Thin posts (minor):** about 250 words each, partly about the demo itself, with only 2 blocks and 1 image per post.
- **Duplicated page shell (minor):** the full HTML head, header and footer are repeated in both page templates instead of a shared layout.

The full write-up is in `results/2026-10-03_1107_mcp_gpt-6-sol-high/grade.md`, and the solution is archived as `refs/runs/2026-10-03_1107_mcp_gpt-6-sol-high`.
